Git Commands: Complete Guide
Windows CMD guide for the classroom-quiz-mern-gemini project and future GitHub uploads
1. Check Git installation
Confirm that Git is installed and available:
git --version
2. Configure your Git identity
git config --global user.name "Rishij4"
git config --global user.email "your-email@example.com"
REM Check saved settings
git config --global user.name
git config --global user.email
Replace your-email@example.com with your actual email address.

Replace your-email@example.com with your actual email address. If you already configured it correctly, you do not need
to repeat these commands.
3. Go to your project folder
cd /d "C:\Users\Asus\Downloads\classroom-quiz-mern-gemini"
4. Initialize Git (already completed)
git init
Run this only when setting up a local repository for the first time; do not repeat it for routine updates.
5. Check status and stage files
git status
git add .
git add filename.

epeat it for routine updates.
5. Check status and stage files
git status
git add .
git add filename.txt
git add . stages all eligible changes. git add filename.txt stages only the named file; replace the example with your actual
filename and path.
6. Commit changes
git commit -m "Initial commit"
git commit -m "Add new file"
Use a message that describes the change. The first command is for the initial commit; the second is an example for a later
change.

7. Branch and GitHub remote setup
git branch -M main
git remote add origin https://github.com/Rishij4/classroom-quiz-mern-gemini.git
git remote -v
git remote set-url origin https://github.com/Rishij4/classroom-quiz-mern-gemini.git
Use git remote add only when no remote named origin exists. Use set-url only if origin already exists and you need to
correct its URL.

correct its URL. Your current project already has the remote configured.
8. Push to GitHub
git push -u origin main
git push
Use git push -u origin main for the first successful upload of the main branch. For later uploads, git push is usually enough.

Page 2
9. View history and changes
git log --oneline
git diff
git pull
git log --oneline shows commit history. git diff shows unstaged changes. git pull fetches and integrates updates from the
remote repository.
10. Everyday workflow: add one more file
cd /d "C:\Users\Asus\Downloads\classroom-quiz-mern-gemini"
git status
git add filename.txt
git commit -m "Add new file"
git push
Replace filename.txt with the actual file name. To stage all eligible project changes instead, use git add .

Important safety reminders
• Do not upload API keys, passwords, or secret credentials.
• Make sure .env files and node_modules are excluded using .gitignore.
• Before committing, run git status and review which files will be included.
• GitHub authentication may open a browser window.
Quick workflow to remember
git status
git add .
git commit -m "Describe your changes"
git push
